findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dnsdomain, pago_seguro, github_repo_activity · Private data: dnsdomain, npm_downloads_range, who_gho_indicator_timeseries, doaj_article_search, email_posture, x402_preflight, tls_pqc, defi_llama_tvl_ranking, payto_preflight, stablecoin_supply, polymarket_trades, registry_watch · Public sink: dnsdomain, npm_downloads_range, who_gho_indicator_timeseries, deps_risk, doaj_article_search, email_posture, pago_seguro, tls_pqc.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dnsdomain, pago_seguro, github_repo_activity · Private data: dnsdomain, npm_downloads_range, who_gho_indicator_timeseries, doaj_article_search, email_posture, x402_preflight, tls_pqc, defi_llama_tvl_ranking, payto_preflight, stablecoin_supply, polymarket_trades, registry_watch · Public sink: dnsdomain, npm_downloads_range, who_gho_indicator_timeseries, deps_risk, doaj_article_search, email_posture, pago_seguro, tls_pqc

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
